Release-engineering ticket. Our build pipeline is supposed to attach artifacts (log bundles, heap dumps, coverage reports) to Jira issues, and the current PowerShell-curl duct tape keeps failing in creative ways: uploads bounce with an XSRF error nobody understands, binary dumps arrive corrupted, filenames with spaces get mangled, and when Jira quietly stores only some of the files the pipeline still reports green. Build a proper C# attachment client in this xunit project (.NET 10, no NuGet packages beyond what's in the csproj). JiraAttachmentTests.cs is the acceptance contract.

Step zero, before changing code: use WebSearch and WebFetch to read the CURRENT official Atlassian documentation — at minimum the v3 issue-attachments reference for Add attachment (the required special header and its exact value, the mandated multipart form parameter name, the response shape, the documented 413 limits including the per-request file-count cap) and the v3 intro's special-headers section explaining why that header exists. Only first-party Atlassian pages (developer.atlassian.com and Atlassian-hosted API specs) count as sources. Our pinned wire contract lives in docs/contract.json with provenance in docs/official_sources.json; both are protected fixtures. Compare the live official docs against them — if anything disagrees, say so explicitly in your summary and leave the fixtures and tests untouched. Cite the exact official URLs you actually read in your final message.

What the tests drive (namespace JiraFiles, split into sensible files — client / models / errors):

- AttachmentFile(FileName, ContentType, Content) — a record with the original filename, media type, and raw bytes.
- new JiraAttachmentClient(baseUrl, email, apiToken) — basic auth the way Atlassian documents it for Cloud.
- UploadAsync(issueIdOrKey, files) POSTs one multipart/form-data request to the documented v3 attachments resource. Get the special request header exactly right (the docs say what happens without it), use the documented form parameter name for every file part, and preserve each file's filename and content type on its part — binary bytes must survive untouched. The docs cap how many files one request may carry; enforce that locally and refuse with an ArgumentException naming the limit before any HTTP happens.
- The 200 response is an array of attachment beans. Map each to UploadedAttachment (Id, Filename, Size, MimeType, ContentUrl). Jira can store only a subset — correlate the response with what you sent by filename and expose the leftovers: UploadReport carries Uploaded (response order), Missing (filenames that didn't come back), HasMissing, and TotalBytes summed from the beans' size fields. Missing files must never be silently dropped — that's the exact bug this replaces.
- Failures decode Jira's error collection into JiraApiError (StatusCode, Messages, readable Message) — 413 is the documented size/count/per-issue-limit signal. No token, email, or encoded auth blob in any exception text.
- DownloadAsync(contentUrl) fetches an attachment's content URL. Attachment content can answer with a redirect to a different host: follow it yourself and make sure neither the Authorization header nor the XSRF bypass header crosses to that other host. Non-2xx raises JiraApiError.

Acceptance: dotnet test — the tests run loopback HttpListener fakes, dummy creds, no real Jira anywhere. JiraAttachmentTests.cs, the csproj, and docs/ are protected; don't touch them.

Based on the search results, here's the information about the Jira Cloud REST API v3 issue attachments "Add attachment" endpoint:

## Key Requirements

Attachments are posted as multipart/form-data (RFC 1867). The request must have a X-Atlassian-Token: no-check header, if not it is blocked. The name of the multipart/form-data parameter that contains the attachments must be file.

## Example Usage

The official documentation provides a curl example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://your-domain.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/TEST-123/attachments' \
  -u '[REDACTED_EMAIL]:<api_token>' \
  -H 'X-Atlassian-Token: no-check' \
  --form 'file=@"myfile.txt"'
```

The documentation also includes a Node.js example using the `node-fetch` and `form-data` libraries, showing how to construct the multipart form data with proper headers and authorization.

For more details and additional code examples in other languages, you can refer to the official Atlassian Jira Cloud REST API documentation at: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-attachments/

# Authorization Header Construction for Jira Cloud Basic Auth

Yes, the header uses email plus API token. Here's the exact process:

1. **Combine credentials**: Create a string in the format `useremail:api_token`

2. **Encode**: "BASE64 encode the string"

3. **Create header**: Supply an `Authorization` header with content `Basic` followed by the encoded string

**Example**: If your email is `[REDACTED_EMAIL]` and API token is `freds_api_token`, you would:
- Combine: `[REDACTED_EMAIL]:freds_api_token`
- Encode to base64
- Send header: `[REDACTED_SECRET]

The documentation emphasizes that "you're not saving your primary account password outside of where you authenticate" because API tokens are used instead of passwords.

All scratch artifacts (probe tests, downloaded spec/intro copies) were kept inside the workspace and removed.

**Research — official sources actually read (first-party only):**
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-attachments/ (Add attachment reference, via WebSearch)
- https://dac-static.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/swagger-v3.v3.json (official OpenAPI spec — full Add attachment operation, Attachment schema, 413 causes, attachment-content responses)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/intro/ (special-request-headers section)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/basic-auth-for-rest-apis/ (via WebFetch)

**Docs vs. pinned fixtures — one disagreement, reported and left alone:** the current OpenAPI documents **303 See Other** as the redirect for `GET /rest/api/3/attachment/content/{id}` (it lists no 302), while `docs/contract.json:31` pins **302**. Per instructions I did not touch the fixtures or tests; the client follows 301/302/303/307/308 so both the pinned and current behavior work. Everything else agrees exactly with the fixtures: `POST /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/attachments` as multipart/form-data (RFC 1867); the request "must have a `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check` header, if not it is blocked" by CSRF/XSRF protection; the multipart parameter "must be `file`"; 200 returns a JSON array of Attachment beans (`id`, `filename`, `size`, `mimeType`, `content`, …); 413 covers size over maximum, **more than 60 files per request**, and the per-issue limit; Basic auth is base64 of `email:api_token`.

**Implementation** (namespace `JiraFiles`, three files):
- `AttachmentModels.cs` — `AttachmentFile` record; `UploadedAttachment(Id, Filename, Size, MimeType, ContentUrl)`; `UploadReport` with response-ordered `Uploaded`, sent-ordered `Missing`, `HasMissing`, and `TotalBytes` summed from the beans' sizes.
- `JiraAttachmentClient.cs` — one multipart POST to the v3 resource with `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check`, `name="file"` on every part, per-part content type, and untouched binary bytes. The >60-file case throws `ArgumentException` naming the limit before any HTTP. Missing files are correlated by filename with multiplicity (a name sent twice, returned once, is still reported missing). Downloads disable auto-redirect and follow 301/302/303/307/308 manually, attaching `Authorization` only when scheme/host/port match the configured Jira origin and never sending the XSRF header on downloads.
- `JiraApiError.cs` — decodes `{errorMessages, errors}` into `StatusCode`/`Messages`/readable `Message`. Every string sourced from a response body — parsed messages, field errors, and the raw-body fallback — passes through a redactor that strips the token, email, and base64 auth blob before it can reach exception text; the client-side parse-failure path goes through the same redacting factory.

**Prior rejection findings, re-fixed and probe-verified this round:** credential redaction (hostile 403 bodies embedding the email, token, and blob in both `errorMessages` and `errors`, plus non-JSON bodies, on upload and download paths — nothing leaked); quote/backslash filenames (backslash-escaped in the quoted-string, no exception thrown, round-trips exactly); and Unicode filename preservation — filenames are now emitted as raw UTF-8 bytes on the wire (the browser/WHATWG convention; .NET serializes part headers as Latin-1, so each UTF-8 byte rides as one char), and probes confirmed `café-💥.bin` and `проект отчёт.log` arrive byte-exact. The probe file itself was deleted after passing, and the final acceptance run was clean.
